summary: Read the checkpoint's sealed set in short pages instead of one long read transaction

replay.detail: No replay or rebuild, and the sealed set, its digest and the checkpoint plan are unchanged for the same claims.

schema.detail: No tables, columns, indexes or triggers.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged. The sealed set and the sealed-identities digest are the same values as before; a test compares the paged reads with a single read at several page sizes, and the checkpoint, tombstone and sealed tests pass.

compatibility.detail: No client, wire or harness contract change.

recovery.detail: The sealed-set and sealed-identities reads held one read transaction for the whole scan, 20 to 36 seconds on a large store, which kept the write-ahead log from being checkpointed and let it grow to hundreds of megabytes. Each now reads in pages of 5,000 envelopes and 20,000 records, each page a read of its own, so the log can be checkpointed between pages. The one difference from a single snapshot: a record that changes state (a repair) between two pages of the same call could be read in either state. The plan-and-prove copy (VACUUM INTO) is now listed among the live reads in the checkpoint log line, but it still reads the whole store in one transaction.
